title: Decision-tree depth of restricted DNF gates
statement:
Fix an integer $n \ge 1$ and a positive integer $l$, and let $\phi_1, \dots, \phi_s$ be DNF formulas on $n$ Boolean variables, each of width at most $l$ and each written so that no variable occurs more than once in any single term — that is, no term repeats a literal, and no term contains two literals on the same variable. Let $p \in \bbr$ satisfy $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40 l}$ (so in particular $p \le 1$). Then a Bernoulli$(p)$ random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables satisfies, with probability at least
\[
  1 - s\left(\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{np}{3}\right)\right),
\]
that for every $i$ the restricted function $x \mapsto \phi_i$ evaluated on the coordinates left free by $\rho$ (with the fixed coordinates set by $\rho$) has decision-tree depth at most $l$.
hypotheses_covered: a family of s DNF formulas on n variables
each DNF has width at most l
within each term, literals on the same variable are identical (no conflicting polarities)
each term has no duplicate literals
replaced:
Under the same hypotheses, a Bernoulli$(p)$ restriction $\rho$ leaves every one of
the $s_i$ width-$\le l$ gates with restricted function of decision-tree depth at
most $l$, with probability at least
$1-s_i\cdot\bigl((1/2)^l+\exp(-np/3)\bigr)$. This is the decision-tree-depth form
of the one-step bound applied with width $l$.
